sources.entry: Chitchatter - Peer-to-peer chat app that is serverless, decentralized, and ephemeral. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Chitchatter is a free, open-source, browser-based peer-to-peer chat app that is end-to-end encrypted via WebRTC, ephemeral, and runs without a central API server.
summary.what_it_does: Chitchatter lets people join rooms in the browser and chat, with peers connecting directly over WebRTC and using public WebTorrent trackers for initial pairing and TURN relays as a fallback. Rooms support multiple peers, public and private rooms, audio and video chat, screen sharing, and direct messages. Files are sent peer-to-peer, encrypted before sending with the room name as the key, and the README says transfers have no size limit. Messages are held only in memory and are cleared when you leave a room. The README also describes Markdown rendering with code syntax highlighting, conversation backfilling for new joiners, automatic peer verification via client-side public-key cryptography, and embedding via an iframe or a Web Component SDK. The project can be forked and self-hosted, for example on GitHub Pages or any static host.
use_cases: Private chat with friends or family
Group coordination for unions or movements
Sharing files or text between devices
Sending sensitive data such as passwords
Embedding a chat room in another web app
how_to_run: In the project directory, run: npm install
Run npm start for the development server (uses public WebTorrent trackers)
Run npm run build to produce a production build in dist
Serve the dist folder from any static host served over a secure context
notable: Serverless design: no API server is needed for basic use, and public WebTorrent and TURN servers handle connection setup
Ephemeral by design: messages are never persisted to disk on client or server
Core chat logic in src/core is platform-agnostic and can run in Node or a terminal
Optional hash-based routing so the room name is not sent to the server
Embeddable as a Web Component SDK with room, user, and colour-mode attributes
caveats: Development is officially supported only on *NIX systems; Windows users are directed to WSL
Peers connect only within the same domain, so forks hosted elsewhere cannot reach the main instance
The developer describes the project as in maintenance mode, and the free TURN relay gives no service guarantees
Some ad blockers and iOS Safari can prevent peers from connecting or rejoining
